changelog: CRITICAL (completeness, SC6): Sessions could never recover a missed Stop-hook — the idle-promotion sweep (§8.3/§10.4) keyed on `ended_at IS NOT NULL AND ended_at < now-IDLE`, but a missed Stop-hook leaves `ended_at` NULL forever, so the predicate excluded exactly the case it claimed to recover. Fix: added a dedicated `sessions.last_activity_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT now()` column refreshed on every `capture_turn`; reserved `ended_at` for explicit close only; re-keyed `idx_sessions_open` and both sweeps (§8.3 and §10.4) to `status='open' AND last_activity_at < now-IDLE`; updated §8.8 missed-Stop-hook bullet and SC6 verification (§1.6); resolved the appendix §8 open question (column semantic now committed).

CRITICAL (security-isolation): Intra-tenant visibility (private/team/world) was promised in §7.5 but enforced nowhere — no Scoped* method injected a visibility/user_id/team_id predicate, so every default-`private` fact was recallable by any other member of the org and the team tier was unenforced (moving namespace=userId→tenantId had dissolved openbrains' only per-user gate). Fix: added `visibilityPredicate({visibility,team_id,user_id})` = `(visibility='world' OR (visibility='team' AND team_id IN p.teamIds) OR (visibility='private' AND user_id=p.userId))` to ScopedDB as an un-omittable part of the Scoped* contract; added `ScopedDB.readFacts` choke-point that always ANDs it; wired it into §8.4 recall, §8.5 get_session_context injection, and the Pillar-2 path (replaced line-157 prose with the choke-point). Stated explicitly that visibility is structural, not a per-op convention.

CRITICAL (security, hybrid arm — caught on advisor review): the visibility leak also rode the hybrid/`think` arm via session-transcript chunks. Fix: added `visibility`/`user_id`/`team_id` columns to the `chunks` DDL (§4.9; ingested-doc chunks default `visibility='world'`, session chunks inherit the session's tier); applied `visibilityPredicate` in `ScopedDB.hydrateChunks` and `getChunksByIds` (§5.3/§7.3); carried `visibility`/`userId` in the §4.3 and §8.3 chunk inserts + Vectorize metadata (making the §8.3 embed-metadata `visibility` load-bearing rather than dangling); updated the §5.2 field-origin map and §7.5 column-coverage note (which previously, incorrectly, said chunks carry no visibility column).

HIGH (cf-correctness, recall cliff): the Vectorize topK ceiling (50 with metadata) + drop-out-of-scope-at-D1 produced a silent recall cliff for restricted-allowedScopes principals (Persona C) — over-fetch capped at 50 cannot cover it. Fix: made the scope/visibility metadata-filtered Vectorize query the PRIMARY path for restricted principals via `ScopedVectorize.foldPartitionFilter` (single-scope grant → {scope} pushed into the filter; multi-scope → one query per scope then union; '*' unchanged); documented metadata-filtered query as required-before-GA for agency tenants; over-fetch demoted to a multi-grant/no-index fallback with a documented eviction bound (§5.3).

HIGH (cf-correctness, D1 write throughput): the scale story reasoned only about bytes (6 GB) and never about D1's single-writer write throughput, even though every read wrote a synchronous recall-trace row. Fix: added a D1 WRITE-THROUGHPUT budget to §10.7 (a second scale axis); decoupled recall-trace writes from the synchronous read path via `ctx.waitUntil`/batched-to-separate-store (audit rows stay in-batch for atomicity, traces need not); added a write-QPS scale-trigger so the shard-split alert fires on EITHER bytes OR write-QPS; updated SC9 (§1.6) to observe both axes and the appendix recall-trace open question.

HIGH (completeness, importer input schemas): the flagship G6/Persona A ChatGPT and Claude-Code importers specified only the ob1 OUTPUT contract, never the INPUT export shapes. Fix: added §4.7.1 specifying the ChatGPT `conversations.json` mapping-tree shape (node/parent walk to linearize turns) and the Claude Code JSONL transcript shape (per-line message records, content-block text extraction), the asRecord/asString field guards (skip-record on drift), the turn→`session_turns` mapping, and the byte/line-offset resumable cursor; pointed §8.2 path 2 at it.

HIGH (completeness, Workflow step cap): a single oversized upload could approach the 10k/25k Workflow step cap (the Enumerator bounds a source, not one document). Fix: added `MAX_CHUNKS_PER_DOC=4000` and a deterministic split rule in §4.3 (oversized doc split at chunk boundaries into multiple `documents` rows sharing `parent_document_id`/`part_index`/`part_count`, each its own Workflow with an idempotent `#part${k}` instance id); added the three columns to the §4.9 `documents` DDL so the rule cites real schema; this makes SC5 'at scale' defensible for the giant-upload case.

MEDIUM (completeness, session-fact dedup): re-promoting an edited/re-run session could insert near-duplicate facts (content_hash skip-unchanged does nothing once the transcript changes). Fix: committed a deterministic v1 supersede-by-source rule at §8.3 writeback — soft-expire the prior promoted fact set for the `source_session_id` (preserving lineage) before inserting, plus an in-batch dedup on `(tenant_id, entity_slug, kind, LOWER(TRIM(fact)))`; updated §8.8 and resolved the appendix §8 open question (no longer a deferral). Cross-session semantic/cosine dedup remains deferred to Phase 3.5.

MEDIUM (completeness, doc-link node space): BFS over `doc_links` was ambiguous — the DDL comment said from_id/to_id were 'pages.id or documents.id (same node space)' but the BFS node table is `pages|entities`. Fix: pinned the DOC_GRAPH node space to `pages` only (documents participate via a backing page, gbrain's model); updated the §6.1 DDL comments, the §6.0 table, added a pinned node-space note, and resolved the appendix §6 open question.

MEDIUM (cf-correctness, reranker output shape): the bge-reranker-base output-field shape is unpinned and the index→chunk remap depends on it (a wrong remap mis-attributes a citation). Fix: promoted the staging integration test that locks the shape to a HARD, named, BLOCKING CI/deploy gate (§10.6 + §5.4), not just 'a staging test'; until green, rerank degrades to RRF order; confirmed shape captured back into §5.4 once locked; appendix updated.

MEDIUM (security, write-side body fields): the webhook `POST /ingest` (and capture_turn/writeFact) did not validate body-supplied scope/team_id/user_id/visibility against the resolved Principal. Fix: §7.3 `writeFact` and §8.2 path-3 now validate through ScopedDB on write — scope must pass `assertScopeAllowed` (else 403), team_id must be in p.teamIds, user_id is forced to p.userId, visibility is role-constrained by `constrainVisibility` (a `world` write requires admin/owner); added §7.10 edge case + canary #11 (write-isolation).

MEDIUM (security, audit/trace read-auth): `memory_audit`/`memory_recall_traces` were scoped tenant-wide with no per-reader gate, letting any member reconstruct other users' queries and surfaced private facts. Fix: §7.6 now restricts `memory_recall_traces` reads to the authoring user_id (owner/admin compliance read, audited) and `memory_audit` reads to owner/admin; added canary #12.

Test suite (§10.6): added blocking canaries #8 (private tier, facts AND chunks), #9 (team tier), #10 (recall-completeness under topK pressure — the complement to the cross-scope leak test), #11 (write-isolation), #12 (audit/trace read-auth), and the reranker output-shape blocking gate; updated SC1 wording (§1.6) to 'zero cross-tenant leak AND enforced cross-scope isolation AND enforced intra-tenant visibility' and the Pillar-4 acceptance test (§1.5).

LOW (cf-correctness, long-chunk rerank truncation): documented and accepted for v1 that a long chunk is reranked on a truncated prefix while synthesized in full (mitigated by the ingest chunk-target keeping most chunks under the cap); recorded as an accepted residual rather than a silent behavior.
residualIssues: DELIVERY/HARNESS LIMIT: the complete edited PRD is 364,381 characters (~97K tokens) — larger than the 327K that already truncated in the prior iteration — so it exceeds a single StructuredOutput model-output ceiling. The full, rebuilt document is durable on disk at `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-roboto-devel/de8de32f-fcde-4884-89d9-eeaaf43cb4da/scratchpad/PRD.md` (assembled by `build.py` from s01–s10 + appendix, every iter-3 edit applied inline). The `prdMarkdown` field emits the full document verbatim and relies on the harness's truncate-and-resume behavior (the prior run 'truncated once and resumed') to deliver §2–§10; no §1+pointer shortcut is used.

CONSCIOUS SCOPING — visibility on chunks: ingested-document chunks default `visibility='world'` (org/team knowledge, recallable tenant-wide) while session-transcript chunks inherit the session's tier. This is the intended v1 model, not a gap: a document author who needs a private document sets its visibility at ingest and it mirrors to chunks. If finer per-paragraph privacy is ever needed it is additive (the predicate already reads the column).

CONSCIOUS SCOPING — owner/admin do NOT bypass `visibilityPredicate` on the recall/think path; a private fact is private even from an admin's recall. Admin reach over private memory is an explicit, audited compliance read surface (§7.6), not the default path. Confirm this matches the intended governance posture (a reviewer could reasonably want admin recall to see all tenant memory).

DEFERRED with rationale — cross-session semantic fact dedup: v1 commits only a deterministic, embedding-free supersede-by-`source_session_id` + exact-normalized-text dedup. gbrain's cosine/classifier dedup (and any cross-session 'this fact restates that one' merge) stays deferred to the Phase-3.5 entity-vector work, consistent with the v1 'no entity vectors / semantic dedup' non-goal. Re-finalize of the SAME session is idempotent; near-duplicate facts ACROSS different sessions are not merged in v1.

ACCEPTED for v1 — long-chunk rerank truncation: a long chunk is reranked on a truncated prefix while synthesized in full, so long chunks can be mildly mis-ranked. Accepted; mitigated by the ingest chunk-target. Revisit only if ranking-quality data shows long-chunk mis-ordering.

PENDING external confirmation (launch dependencies, not design gaps) — (a) the exact bge-reranker-base output field names, locked by the now-blocking staging gate before the index→chunk remap is trusted in prod; (b) the exact current Workers AI per-model request-RATE limits for the v1 models, with a limit-increase request filed pre-launch if the fleet projection exceeds them; (c) the concrete `idle_minutes` idle-promotion window and re-embed pacing values, tuned once Phase-4 load is characterized.

TUNING (not v1 blockers): trust-grade boost values (instruction 2.0 / evidence 1.0 / draft 0.6) and the COSINE_FLOOR/rerank thresholds are placeholders needing empirical tuning against real ranking data; the recall-trace retention window N and the D1 write-QPS shard-split threshold are committed-as-policy but their exact numbers await Phase-4 load.
